title: Automotive QFN, AEC-Q100 grade 1, derivative package
authored_by: hand-written expectation, not a snapshot of generator output
rationale: Grade 1 escalation: TC must run the -55/+125 C class condition for 1000 cycles with a 500-cycle interim readpoint, and HTSL must reach 1000 h at 150 C. A consumer-grade 500-cycle / 500-hour plan is a fail for this scenario.
Automotive lot floor: 3 non-consecutive assembly lots even though the novelty is 'derivative'. A plan that emits 1 lot here has leveraged similarity further than an automotive customer will accept.
Pd-coated Cu wire on Al pads: biased HAST is the leg that finds halide-driven IMC corrosion. It must be present and must not be silently replaced by THB.

Automotive mechanical suite: mechanical shock and variable-frequency vibration are required rows; constant acceleration is historically a cavity/hermetic test so it is expected only as a CONDITIONAL row with a TODO.

QFN is a leadframe package, not an area array: board-level DROP must not appear (no handheld exposure, no CSP joint), and solder BALL shear must not appear (there are no balls). Board-level TC of the exposed-pad joint is legitimate but conditional.
Wire-bond construction keeps wire pull and ball-bond shear in scope, with readpoints tied to HTSL so IMC degradation is caught mechanically before it is caught electrically.
